explanation: The cardinals' ballots are burned in a stove after voting, with chemicals added so the colour shows clearly. Black smoke means no one has yet won enough votes.

claims.text: White smoke from the Sistine Chapel chimney signals that a new pope has been elected.
Black smoke means that no pope has yet been elected; red and gold smoke are not part of the signal.
The cardinals' ballots are burned in a stove after voting, with chemicals added to colour the smoke.

evidence.restatement: White smoke from the Sistine Chapel chimney announces that a pope has been elected.
Black smoke means a ballot without a result; there is no red or gold signal.
The ballots are burned in a stove in the Sistine Chapel, and chemical cartridges are added so the smoke is clearly black or white.
White smoke from the Sistine Chapel chimney announces that a pope has been elected.
Black smoke means no pope yet; there is no red or gold smoke signal.
The ballots are burned in a stove and chemicals are added to colour the smoke.
